title: We put Claude with our MCP against Scalar Field and Conviction on the same trading questions
author: Wendy_Trade
selftext:
Disclosure up front: we built Wendy, an MCP server that does the market math for Claude, ChatGPT and Robinhood Agents. We wanted to see how the "AI does the math through a tool" approach holds up against standalone AI trading apps, so we ran a side-by-side against two YC companies, Scalar Field and Conviction.

We typed the same questions into both sides, screen recorded everything and timed each answer from the moment it got the question. The questions covered support and resistance, SPY and SPX gamma exposure, multi-indicator reads on AAPL, QQQ and BTC, session type, expected range and breaks of structure.

Against Scalar Field, Claude with Wendy had a median of 24.5 seconds on analysis questions vs 73 seconds. Scalar showed "Something went off track" three times and refused the SPX expected range question after about two minutes. Where both finished, the numbers matched, and AAPL agreed on 9 of 10 indicators to the cent.

Against Conviction, typical speed was about the same (21 vs 22 seconds median). Conviction had 3 blank or stalled answers and 4 partial or full refusals, mostly on options and SPX. It told us it didn't have SPX and answered "in SPY terms" instead.

Each of them beat us on something. Scalar Field was quicker at setting up alerts, which we don't offer yet, and Conviction gave a better answer on the economic calendar.

The bigger takeaway for anyone building in this space is that the failures came from wrong inputs (SPY for SPX, realized vol for implied), stale data and refusals rather than bad arithmetic. Getting the data layer right seems to matter more than the model.

We ran this on October 26, 2026, and the full round-by-round tables are on our sub: https://www.reddit.com/r/WendyTrade/

Happy to answer questions about how we ran it.

comments.author: alittlebitnostalgic
comments.body: The data quality point is true. Even a good model can't give reliable answers if the inputs are wrong or outdated.

replies.author: Wendy_Trade
replies.body: Yeah, that ended up being most of the story for us. SPX was the clearest case: if a tool doesn't have the SPX chain, it either refuses or answers in SPY terms, and the math on top can be perfect and still point at the wrong levels. That's why we pull SPX gamma from the SPX chain itself.

comments.author: investigatormaker
comments.body:
The SPX-for-SPY substitutions warrant a separate comparison from answer speed: a fast answer about the wrong instrument isn't equivalent coverage. Beside each recording, include the requested instrument, data timestamp and whether the answer actually used it, so traders evaluating Wendy can inspect those failures. Keep Scalar's alert advantage and Conviction's calendar advantage visible; neither latency nor matching indicator values settles which workflow someone needs. Our Reddit work would answer traders asking how to give Claude market calculations, explaining Wendy's tool-based approach and the limits your comparison identifies.
